summary: Frontend-only testing of redesigned /shop page. All 14 spec features verified end-to-end on desktop and mobile: intro headline + left filter rail + masonry grid, results-count '14 invitations', all 8 category buttons with counts (Embossed 3, Floral 2, Minimal 2, Foil 2, Botanical 2, Classic 2, Duo 1), URL sync (?category=<X>, category-all clears), deep-link (/shop?category=Foil pre-filters to 2), live search (foil→2, elodie→1), sort options (asc first='The Lin' vs desc first='The Solene'), favorites toggle + Saved (N) + localStorage 'ewc-favorites' persistence across reload, load-more (14 items, PAGE_SIZE=8 → 'Show 6 more' then disappears), right slide-over product-drawer with #card= URL hash, WhatsApp href https://wa.me/910000000000..., thumbs (thumb-0/1), 3 Elodie variants (variant-0/1/2 with prices updating incl. ₹130 Antique Silver), fullscreen gallery-lightbox open/close, Adelaide Duo pair pricing ₹190 / pair on tile AND in drawer, breadcrumb-home -> '/', all product images loaded (11/11 in shop, 10/10 on landing after scroll), mobile 390x844 drawer is truly full-width (x=0, w=390) with filter rail wrapping above grid. Landing page regression clean.
critical_code_review_comments: WHATSAPP_NUMBER = '910000000000' is a placeholder — replace with real number before production.
Shop.jsx is ~605 lines; consider extracting ProductDrawer and GalleryLightbox into their own components for readability (nice-to-have, not blocking).
Image alt text uses c.id (product name) which is acceptable but could be more descriptive for a11y.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Shop redesign iteration_4 fully passes. Testids in place: shop-page, results-count, category-{all|embossed|floral|minimal|foil|botanical|classic|duo}, sort-{featured|price-asc|price-desc}, shop-search-input, favorites-toggle, favorite-<slug>, product-card-<slug>, product-drawer, drawer-{close|whatsapp|share|favorite|enlarge}, thumb-<idx>, variant-<idx>, gallery-lightbox, gallery-close, load-more-btn, breadcrumb-home, empty-state. WhatsApp number is a placeholder — do not treat as bug.
